# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in contributing to this project! We welcome contributions from everyone. To make the process smooth and predictable, please follow these guidelines.

## Getting started

1. Fork the repository and create a branch from the default branch:
   - git checkout -b <your-branch-name>
2. Make small, focused changes with clear commit messages.
3. Run tests and linters locally before opening a PR.

## Branch naming

Use readable branch names, for example:
- feature/add-thing
- fix/bug-description
- chore/docs-update

## How to open an issue

- Search existing issues first to avoid duplicates.
- Provide a clear title and a short description of the problem or feature.
- For bugs include steps to reproduce, expected behavior, and actual behavior.

## How to open a pull request

- Rebase or merge the latest main branch into your branch.
- Provide a clear description of what you changed and why.
- Link any related issues (e.g. Fixes #123).
- Ensure tests pass and include new tests if appropriate.
- Use the repository’s PR template.

## Code style

- Python: follow PEP8 (we recommend using Black and isort).
- Keep functions small and focused.
- Write tests for new functionality.

## Review process

- PRs will be reviewed by maintainers; please be responsive to review feedback.
- We may request changes — once addressed, update the PR for follow-up review.

## Communication

If you have questions before working on a change, open an issue or reach out via GitHub Discussions if available.

Thank you for contributing!
